ux.purpose: Publish, export, preview and SEO — turning what is in the editor into a live deployment (or a downloadable copy of the code), and telling the user what is about to go out, what did go out, and what to do when it doesn't.
ux.task: Publish a site that has been published before
ux.finding: On every fresh load of a site that has ever been published, the Publish panel opens claiming 'Published to production.' and its own primary button — 'Publish to production' — is DISABLED. The panel decides 'nothing to send' from `snapshot.changeCount`, which counts entries in the in-session undo stack; HistoryManager wipes that stack on every PROJECT_LOADED, so it is 0 on load no matter how much unpublished work exists. `justPublished` is therefore true on arrival, which also HIDES the two sections that would have shown the truth (SINCE LAST DEPLOY and LAST DEPLOY). A user who edited yesterday, saved and came back today is told their work is live and is refused the button that would make it so. The only way to re-enable it is to make one more edit in this session, or leave the panel and use the topbar.
ux.evidence: PublishTab.tsx:222 (`justPublished = uiState === 'published' && snapshot.changeCount === 0`), :462 (success section), :549 and :602 (both 'what would go out' sections gated on `!justPublished`), :698 (`disabled={isPublishing || justPublished || snapshot.error}`); usePublishSnapshot.ts:156-166 (changes read from `composer.history.getHistoryStack()`); HistoryManager.ts:155-159 (undoStack/redoStack reset on PROJECT_LOADED), :658-660; usePublishJob.ts:299-311 (hydratedUrl alone yields uiState 'published'). Searched: 'justPublished', 'changeCount', 'getHistoryStack', 'hasUnpublishedChanges'.
ux.fix: Derive 'is anything waiting to ship?' from the same durable signal the topbar uses (saved-at vs last-published-at, plus the server's hasUnpublishedChanges) — never from a per-session undo stack. Keep the CTA enabled whenever the answer is unknown; a republish of identical content is harmless, a refused publish of real work is not. Reserve the 'Published to production' success beat for a publish that finished in THIS session.

ux.task: Decide whether there is anything to publish
ux.finding: The two publish surfaces on screen at the same time answer 'is there anything to publish?' from different data and print opposite answers. The topbar computes it from this session's save clock against last-published-at, falling back to the server's flag, and renders 'Publish changes'. The panel computes it from the in-session undo stack and prints 'Nothing has changed since the last deploy.' Site-level edits make the split worse: `setProjectSettings` marks the project dirty but records no history entry, so changing the SEO title template, the favicon or the default OG image moves the topbar to 'Publish changes' and leaves the panel at '0 changes'.
ux.evidence: StudioHeader.tsx:592-596 (`hasUnpublishedChanges = isDirty || savedAtMs > publishedAtMs || serverHasUnpublishedChanges`), :615-620; usePublishSnapshot.ts:156-166, :181; PublishTab.tsx:576-586; Composer.ts:785 (`markDirty()` on setProjectSettings, no history record); lifecycle.ts:111-127 (`publishMove` label). Searched: 'hasUnpublishedChanges', 'changeCount', 'serverHasUnpublishedChanges', 'markDirty'.
ux.fix: One source of truth for 'unpublished changes', shared by the topbar and the panel. The panel's change LIST can stay session-scoped, but it must be labelled as such ('changes in this session') and must never be the thing that decides whether publishing is offered.

ux.purpose: Publish, export, preview and SEO — turning what is in the editor into a live deployment (or a downloadable copy of the code), and telling the user what is about to go out, what did go out, and what to do when it doesn't.
ux.task: Wait for a publish to finish
ux.finding: If a status poll fails — a dropped connection, a session timeout, a 500 — the editor stops polling and strands the user inside the in-progress state with no way out. The poll error is written to `error`, but the last known job status is still BUILDING, so `uiState` stays 'publishing'; the panel's failure block only renders when uiState is 'failed', so nothing red appears. The progress bar freezes at its last value, the 'started Xs ago' timer keeps counting up forever, and the CTA stays disabled — so the user cannot retry, cannot cancel, and cannot start a fresh publish. The same shape occurs if the worker lambda dies mid-build: the job row never reaches a terminal state, and the server's stale-job cleanup only runs when a NEW publish is attempted, which this panel will not let the user attempt. Reloading the editor is the only escape, and nothing on screen suggests it.
ux.evidence: usePublishJob.ts:155-170 (tick catch → setError + stopPolling), :299-311 (uiState still 'publishing' because status.status is BUILDING); PublishTab.tsx:226 (`hasFailed` requires uiState 'failed'), :245-262 (elapsed timer), :698 (CTA disabled while publishing); publish.service.ts:113-119 + :198-232 (STALE_BUILDING_AFTER_MS cleanup runs only inside startPublish). Searched: 'stopPolling', 'POLL_INTERVAL_MS', 'uiState', 'hasFailed'.
ux.fix: Give the wait a ceiling and an exit. Surface a poll failure as its own state ('Lost contact with the deploy — it may still be running') with Retry and Check status actions; after a bounded timeout, stop claiming progress and offer 'Start over'. Never leave the primary action disabled on a state the user cannot leave.

ux.task: Publish when the publish feature flag is off
ux.finding: When the publish feature flag is off the editor gives two different, mutually exclusive reasons for the same state. The rail still shows Publish (shortcut U) and the panel it opens says 'Connect Vercel to publish.' with a 'Connect Vercel' button that opens the dashboard's integrations page — where a workspace that IS connected will read 'connected', leaving the user with a fixed problem and a panel that still refuses. The topbar, from the same state, says 'Publishing isn't switched on for this workspace yet'. This is not a rare configuration: the flag is read as VITE_FEATURE_PUBLISH ?? NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_PUBLISH, and only the NEXT_PUBLIC_ half reaches the shipping editor, so a flag set for the standalone demo alone lands every real user in exactly this panel.

Searched: 'FEATURE_PUBLISH', 'isFeatureEnabled', 'noPublishPath', 'canPublish'.
ux.fix: Separate the three states the panel currently merges — feature off, no Vercel connection, and 'connection lost' — and give each its own sentence and its own action. When publishing is off for the workspace, say so and offer the door that turns it on (or nothing at all); do not send the user to reconnect an integration that is not the problem.

ux.task: Publish a site with a collection that generates a page per entry
ux.finding: Every CMS-generated detail page ships the TEMPLATE page's identity. `generateDynamicPages` clones the template's HTML whole — head included — and then appends a second `<title>` and a second `<meta name="description">` immediately before `</head>` without removing the first. Browsers and search engines take the FIRST title, so a hundred generated pages all announce themselves as the template ('Menu | Acme'), and the template's og:title, og:description, twitter:title and twitter:description ride along untouched — so every shared link previews as the template page. (Canonical and og:url survive this: the editor's export emits neither, so the server injects a correct per-path one. It is the title and the social card that are wrong.) Worse, when the collection's SEO title field is left blank the appended tag is literally `<title></title>` — a second, empty title. Nothing in the editor previews a generated page or warns about any of this.
ux.evidence: cms.service.ts:206-215 (seoTitle/seoDescription appended before `</head>`, template head kept); publish-html.ts:83-105 (`injectSeoTags` guards canonical and og:url with a regex and adds nothing else); ExportEngine.ts:829 (template HTML carries the injector's full head); SEOInjector.ts:133 (`<title>`), :150-171 (og:title / twitter:title). Searched: 'generateDynamicPages', 'pageSeoTitle', '</head>', 'injectSeoTags'.
ux.fix: Replace the template's head identity for a generated page rather than appending to it — one title, one description, one og:title/twitter:title derived from the entry. Give the collection's page-generation settings a preview of one real entry's rendered head so the user can see what a detail page will say before it ships.

ux.task: Download the site as code
ux.finding: The only reachable export path in the editor swallows its own failures. Both ZIP and React handlers in the export modal catch to a dev-only console logger; there is no toast, no inline error, and the button returns from its spinner as if it had worked — so a user whose export died on an unreachable asset or a browser memory limit sees a modal that just... finishes, with no file. The path that DOES toast 'Export complete' / 'Export failed' is orphaned: StudioHeader still receives `onExportHTML` and never calls it, and the site menu's 'Export code' row was re-pointed at the modal, so `handleExportHTML` has no caller at all.
ux.evidence: ExportModal.tsx:120-139 (handleDownloadZip catch → devError only), :141-164 (React path, same); no `useToast`/`addToast` import in the file; useExportHandlers.ts:82-103 (the toasted implementation), :219 (still exported); StudioHeader.tsx:113 + :201 (onExportHTML destructured and never referenced again), :814-823 (the comment recording the re-point); AquibraStudio.tsx:520. Searched: 'handleExportHTML', 'downloadZip', 'addToast', 'devError'.
ux.fix: Every download door reports its own outcome — success with the filename, failure with the reason and a retry. Then delete the orphaned handler or re-point it; two export implementations with different feedback is how one of them ends up being the silent one.

ux.task: Check the site before publishing it
ux.finding: Preview cannot show what a visitor gets, on the surface whose entire job is to show what a visitor gets. Three things stack up: the sanitizer strips every `<script>` and every `<form>` from the document; the iframe is then rendered with `sandbox=""`, which disables scripts, forms and navigation outright; and the overlay renders one combined document with no page switcher, so internal links cannot be followed and multi-page navigation — the single most common thing to check before going live — cannot be checked at all. The engine deliberately ships the interaction runtime into this document so click animations work in preview; it is removed twice over before it can run.
ux.evidence: ExportUtils.ts:35-42 (`querySelectorAll('script,iframe,object,embed,link,meta[http-equiv],base,form')` → remove); PreviewOverlay.tsx:104-109 (`sandbox=""` on the srcDoc iframe), :99-114 (device switcher and Done are the only controls); Composer.ts:694-703 (interaction runtime deliberately embedded for preview), :707-719 (combined = the ACTIVE page). Searched: 'sandbox', 'sanitizeHTMLForPreview', 'UI_TOGGLE_PREVIEW', 'buildInteractionRuntimeScript'.
ux.fix: Decide what preview is FOR and build that. If it is 'see the real site', it needs a page switcher, working internal links and the interaction runtime allowed to run (a scripts-only sandbox on content the editor itself produced). If it must stay inert, say so on screen — 'links and forms are disabled in preview' — instead of showing a page that quietly does nothing when clicked.

ux.task: Read the pre-publish checklist before publishing
ux.finding: The pre-publish checklist can read 'All checks pass.' over a publish the server will refuse. `runPrePublishChecks` reports six things — Vercel, Pages ready, SEO configured, Domain, Empty pages, Favicon — and the client-approval gate is not among them. In an approval-required workspace the server refuses with APPROVAL_NONE / PENDING / CHANGES / STALE, and by then the wizard has already closed (Publish now calls onClose() before onPublish()). The panel behind it does not change state at all — the block is routed to `blockedReason`, not to `error`, so the failure section never renders — and the entire feedback is a 6-second toast. A user who looks away has no record that anything happened.
ux.evidence: publish.service.ts:18-108 (the six checks; no approval check), :248-300 (the approval gate that actually refuses), :108 (`ready = !hasFail`); PublishWizard.tsx:200-215 ('All checks pass.'), :267-274 (onClose() then onPublish()); usePublishJob.ts:204-213 (block → blockedReason, not error); useExportHandlers.ts:163-170 (a toast is the whole response). Searched: 'runPrePublishChecks', 'blockedReason', 'APPROVAL_', 'PUBLISH_APPROVAL_MESSAGES'.
ux.fix: Put the approval gate on the checklist as a row with the same severity vocabulary as the rest, so it can be seen before the button is pressed. Keep the wizard open on a refusal and show the reason and the next move in it; a decision the user must act on does not belong in a toast.

ux.task: Find out which step of a publish failed
ux.finding: The build log names the wrong step, every time. On any failure the worker writes `buildSteps(0, true)` — which marks step 0 'Generating pages' as failed and the other four as pending — regardless of where the run actually died. The panel then renders that list verbatim, so a deploy that failed while talking to Vercel reports 'Generating pages ✕ failed' and 'Deploying to CDN · not run'. The one disclosure surface built to answer 'where did it break' gives a confidently wrong answer.
ux.evidence: packages/dashboard/app/api/workers/publish/[jobId]/route.ts:43-51 (`buildSteps`), :201 (`steps: buildSteps(0, true)` in the catch); PublishTab.tsx:230 (`failedSteps`), :374-400 (the rendered log), :850-856 (STEP_WORD). Searched: 'buildSteps', 'steps:', 'View log', 'failedSteps'.
ux.fix: Record the index of the step that was running when the error was thrown and mark that one failed; leave the steps before it as they were. If the failing step genuinely cannot be identified, say 'the run stopped' rather than blaming step one.

ux.purpose: Publish, export, preview and SEO — turning what is in the editor into a live deployment (or a downloadable copy of the code), and telling the user what is about to go out, what did go out, and what to do when it doesn't.
ux.task: Watch a publish in progress
ux.finding: The 'step N of M' line the progress section was built for never renders. The worker writes the running step with status 'active'; the panel looks for status 'running'. `runningStep` is therefore always null and the line silently falls back to a bare percentage, so the user is told '40%' and never 'Deploying to CDN'. The same vocabulary mismatch reaches the failure log: the worker's 'skipped' has no entry in STEP_WORD, so the two steps that are deliberately not run print the raw word 'skipped' next to steps that say 'done' and 'not run'.
ux.evidence: packages/dashboard/app/api/workers/publish/[jobId]/route.ts:45 (`status: failed ? 'failed' : 'active'`), :34-37 (SKIPPED_STEPS → 'skipped'); PublishTab.tsx:236-241 (`steps.findIndex((s) => s.status === 'running')`), :513-521, :850-856 (STEP_WORD has pending/running/done/failed only); PublishService.ts:30 (the type repeats 'running'). Searched: 'running', 'active', 'STEP_WORD', 'buildSteps'.
ux.fix: Agree one vocabulary for step status across the worker, the transport type and the panel, and cover every value the worker can emit. Until then the progress line should name the phase it can prove rather than a percentage with no noun.

ux.task: Stop a publish that was started by mistake
ux.finding: There is no way to cancel a publish from the editor. Cancellation is built end to end — the hook exposes `cancel`, PublishService calls `sites.cancelPublish`, the router accepts it and the worker checks for CANCELLED between every step — and no control in the editor calls any of it. Once 'Publish now' is pressed the deploy runs to completion whatever the user notices in the next two seconds, and the panel's only interactive element during the run is the disabled CTA.
ux.evidence: usePublishJob.ts:97 (cancel in the result type), :228-236 (implementation, no caller); PublishService.ts:118-126; packages/dashboard/app/api/workers/publish/[jobId]/route.ts:247-253 (checkCancelled between steps). Searched (four spellings): 'publishJob.cancel', 'cancelPublish', 'onCancelPublish', 'cancel deploy' / 'stop publish' / 'abort publish' — zero UI call sites.
ux.fix: Put a Cancel action in the in-progress state, next to the progress bar, and give the cancelled outcome its own panel state (see UX-E-10). The confirm step is the last stop today, and it is one click away from an irreversible action with no undo.

ux.task: Understand why a publish stopped
ux.finding: 'cancelled' is a state the publish machine can reach and no screen draws. The panel branches on publishing / published / failed only, so a job that ends CANCELLED — which today can only arrive from outside the editor — makes the progress section vanish and the panel silently return to its resting state with no statement that a publish was stopped or that nothing was deployed.
ux.evidence: usePublishJob.ts:28-33 (PublishUiState includes 'cancelled'), :304-306; PublishTab.tsx:150 (isPublishing), :155 (isPublished), :226 (hasFailed) — no 'cancelled' branch anywhere in the file. Searched: 'cancelled', 'CANCELLED', 'uiState ===' across editor/.
ux.fix: Give cancelled its own state with the two facts a user needs — the run stopped, and nothing changed on the live site — plus the way back in (Publish again).

ux.task: Export a multi-page site
ux.finding: The export modal previews one page and downloads a different thing depending on which chip is selected, and never says so. The Preview tab, the Code tab and the size/element stats all come from `engine.export()`, which renders the ACTIVE page only. Picking HTML downloads that one page as `index.html` — so a twelve-page site with 'About' open exports About, named index.html, with no warning that eleven pages were dropped. Picking ZIP silently switches to every page, while the preview above it still shows only one. The format blurb ('One HTML file with styles inlined') discloses the count but not that the file is whichever page happened to be open.

ux.task: Check a page that uses background images
ux.finding: Any element with a background image renders unstyled in Preview. The preview sanitizer treats the substring 'url(' as a forbidden style token, and when it matches it removes the ENTIRE style attribute — not the one declaration — and drops any whole `<style>` block that contains one. The preview document carries element styles inline by design, so a hero with a background image loses its size, colour, spacing and typography along with its image, and the user is looking at a broken layout that will not appear on the published site.
ux.evidence: ExportUtils.ts:12 (`FORBIDDEN_STYLE_TOKENS = ['expression', 'url(']`), :56-61 (style ATTRIBUTE removed wholesale on a match), :70-76 (a whole `<style>` block filtered out on a match); Composer.ts:668-672 (the preview document carries element styles inline); ElementManager.ts:444-446 (`setStyle('background-image', 'url(...)')`). Searched: 'FORBIDDEN_STYLE_TOKENS', 'url(', 'background-image', 'sanitizeHTMLForPreview'.
ux.fix: Filter declarations, not whole attributes and stylesheets — an image URL is the normal case on a website builder, not an attack. Whatever is dropped for safety should be reported once at the top of the preview rather than silently changing the design.

ux.task: Publish a site containing a hidden or password-protected page
ux.finding: The visibility control says two opposite things in two adjacent lines. Setting a page to Hidden or Password shows a helper reading 'Not published. Hidden pages are left out of the deploy... a password page is left out too' — and directly under it, a second helper that says 'Page is not linked in menus but reachable via direct URL' or 'Visitors must enter a password to view this page'. The second is false: the exporter drops both kinds before the deploy is assembled. A user reading the nearer sentence believes they have shipped a protected page and has shipped nothing.

ux.task: Publish a collection that generates one page per entry
ux.finding: A collection can be fully configured to generate pages and contribute nothing to the deploy, silently. The template is identified by a free-text 'Template page path' the user types (placeholder: 'blog/_template/index.html'), and at publish time the server matches it by exact string equality against the exported page paths — which the exporter names '<slug>.html'. Any mismatch, including the shape shown in the placeholder, means the collection is skipped with no error: the publish succeeds, the checklist stays green, and the detail pages simply are not there. Nothing in the publish flow counts, names or warns about generated pages.
ux.evidence: CMSCollectionSetupModal.tsx:439-441 (the free-text path field and its placeholder); cms.service.ts:229-247 (`pages.find((p) => p.path === col.pageTemplatePath)`; `if (!template) continue`); ExportEngine.ts:716 (`this.pageHrefs.get(page.id) ?? 'index.html'`); ContentViews.tsx:628-635 (the code already records this trap in a comment). Searched: 'pageTemplatePath', 'appendDynamicPagesToPublish', 'pageSlugPattern', 'pageHrefs'.
ux.fix: Make the template a picker over the real page list, not a typed path, and show the generated-page count in the same place the publish counts pages. A collection that will contribute zero pages belongs on the pre-publish checklist as a warning.

ux.task: Confirm what is about to go live
ux.finding: The number the user approves is not the number that deploys. The confirm step's 'Pages' row is the exporter's count, taken in the browser; the server then appends one generated page per published CMS entry before the job is even created. On a site with a blog collection the user reads 'Pages: 4', presses Publish now, and forty files are uploaded. Nothing anywhere in the editor shows the real deploy manifest.
ux.evidence: PublishConfirmFacts.tsx:118-138 (count from `exportPublishPages`), :162-167 (the Pages row); exportPublishPages.ts:38-49; publish.service.ts:329 (`appendDynamicPagesToPublish` runs server-side, after the count the user saw); cms.service.ts:229-247. Searched: 'onPageCount', 'exportPublishPages', 'appendDynamicPagesToPublish', 'finalPages'.
ux.fix: State the deploy manifest, not the editor's page list: 'N pages + M generated from Blog'. If the generated count can only be known server-side, ask for it before the confirm renders rather than showing a number that is reliably wrong on exactly the sites where it matters.

ux.task: Know whether the site is actually live
ux.finding: A simulated publish is indistinguishable from a real one in the editor. When the simulation escape hatch is enabled the worker walks all five steps on a timer, marks the job COMPLETED and stores a URL on the reserved `.dev-simulated.invalid` domain. The editor then does what it does for a real deploy: toasts 'Published — site is live' with the URL and a 'View live' button that opens an address that can never resolve, and the panel prints 'Published to production.' Nothing on either surface says the deploy was simulated.
ux.evidence: packages/dashboard/app/api/workers/publish/[jobId]/route.ts:406-440 (runSimulation), :100-105 (the opt-in flag), :117-143 (COMPLETED + site.publishedUrl written either way); publish.service.ts:312-315 (the Vercel precheck is skipped under the same flag); useExportHandlers.ts:175-185 ('Published — site is live' + View live); PublishTab.tsx:462-476. Searched: 'PUBLISH_ALLOW_SIMULATION', 'runSimulation', 'dev-simulated', 'publishedUrl'.
ux.fix: Carry the deploy mode back to the client and say it on the success state — 'Simulated publish — nothing was deployed' — and suppress the View-live action when the URL cannot resolve. A success message that cannot be told apart from the real one is the failure mode this flag was supposed to make visible.

ux.task: Understand why a publish failed
ux.finding: Two server conditions reach the user as raw internal strings or as the wrong category. WORKER_DISPATCH_FAILED is not translated by the router, so it falls through as itself and the panel renders 'Publish failed. WORKER_DISPATCH_FAILED Nothing was deployed.' And ALREADY_PUBLISHING — which is not a failure, it means another publish is running right now — is returned as an error, so the editor paints the full red failure block over a deploy that is very much still in progress, and offers 'Try again', which will hit the same conflict.
ux.evidence: server/trpc/routers/sites.ts:339-345 (ALREADY_PUBLISHING → CONFLICT with a message), :371-383 (approval messages), then bare `throw e` for everything else; publish.service.ts:369-383 (WORKER_DISPATCH_FAILED thrown); usePublishJob.ts:204-213 (unclassified message → error → uiState 'failed'); PublishTab.tsx:333-346 (the failure block appends 'Nothing was deployed.'); useExportHandlers.ts:206-215 (generic toast with a Try-again door). Searched: 'WORKER_DISPATCH_FAILED', 'ALREADY_PUBLISHING', 'classifyPublishBlock', 'throw e'.
ux.fix: Translate every error the publish path can produce into a sentence and a next move, and give 'already publishing' its own non-failure state that points at the run in flight rather than offering a retry that cannot succeed.

summary.purpose: Publish, export, preview and SEO — turning what is in the editor into a live deployment (or a downloadable copy of the code), and telling the user what is about to go out, what did go out, and what to do when it doesn't.
summary.finding: PURPOSE. This module is the product's terminal act: it turns the document in the editor into something other people can see — a deployment on the customer's own Vercel account, or a downloaded copy of the code — and it owns the metadata (title, description, social card, canonical, robots, sitemap) that decides how that result is found and shared. PRIMARY TASKS: (1) check the site before shipping — pre-publish checklist and preview; (2) publish, and watch it land; (3) recover when it does not — read the failure, retry, roll back, or take the site down; (4) export the site as HTML/ZIP/React; (5) set the SEO and social fields, per site and per page. ENTRY POINTS: the topbar's single lifecycle CTA (fast path: Confirm modal → deploy); the rail's Publish panel, shortcut U (slow path: panel → two-step wizard → deploy); the site menu ('Publish panel', 'Publish history', 'Export code', 'Share preview link', 'View live site', 'Copy live URL'); Settings › Export ('Open exporter'); the topbar eye and ⌘K for Preview; Pages › page settings › SEO/Social and Settings › SEO for the fields. EXIT POINTS: the live URL (new tab), the dashboard's integrations page (Connect Vercel), the dashboard's share-draft modal, a downloaded file, and History › Published for rollback. HANDS OFF TO: Review (the approval gate that can refuse a publish, and the panel the refusal toast points at), Settings (every 'Fix ›' on a failing check), Pages (page count, visibility, per-page SEO), Content/CMS (generated detail pages appended server-side), History (rollback and version compare), and the dashboard (Vercel connection, domains, favicon, robots, canonical domain, billing plan for the Free badge). RECEIVES FROM: the engine's export pipeline (the page HTML that is deployed), the history stack (its change list), the review service (the approval line), and the server's pre-publish checks. THE SHAPE OF THE DAMAGE: the flow has been carefully built at the level of individual screens and is broken at the level of the seams between them. Three separate 'is anything waiting to ship' answers (undo stack, save clock, server stamps) disagree in the same window; the checklist measures six things and the server refuses on a seventh; the worker and the panel disagree on the word for a running step and on which step failed; the preview, the Google preview and the export modal each show something the deploy will not produce; and the two publish doors — topbar and panel — offer different gates, different recovery affordances and different explanations of the same blocked state. The redesign's job here is not new screens: it is making one publish flow with one truth about state, one vocabulary for progress and failure, and one door back from every way it can go wrong.
summary.evidence: Whole-module read: PublishTab.tsx, PublishWizard.tsx, PublishConfirmFacts.tsx, usePublishSnapshot.ts, usePublishJob.ts, useExportHandlers.ts, exportPublishPages.ts, StudioHeader.tsx, lifecycle.ts, SiteMenu.tsx, PreviewOverlay.tsx, PublishConfirmModal.tsx, ExportModal.tsx, ExportOptions.tsx, ExportUtils.ts, ExportEngine.ts, SEOInjector.ts, SeoScreen.tsx, SeoTab.tsx, SocialTab.tsx, AdvancedTab.tsx, TabRouter.tsx, tabsConfig.ts, services/PublishService.ts; server/services/publish.service.ts, server/services/cms.service.ts, server/trpc/routers/sites.ts, lib/publish-files.ts, lib/publish-html.ts, lib/publish-urls.ts, packages/dashboard/app/api/workers/publish/[jobId]/route.ts. Re-verified against the brief: a publish DOES emit sitemap.xml (publish-files.ts:82-84) and SEOInjector DOES emit canonical/OG/Twitter (SEOInjector.ts:141-150) — both confirmed. One correction to the brief's framing: on CMS-generated pages the canonical and og:url are NOT the template's (the editor emits neither, so publish-html.ts:88-97 injects a correct per-path pair); what IS the template's is the first <title>, og:title, og:description and twitter:* — see UX-E-05.
summary.fix: Rebuild the publish flow around one state machine with one publishable/not-publishable answer, one progress vocabulary shared with the worker, and a named recovery path out of every terminal and stuck state. Merge the topbar and panel gates into one. Make preview, the Google preview and the export preview all render from the deploy pipeline, so no surface can certify output the deploy will not produce.
